audit_findings.title: Contract-acquisition cash reinvestment may be omitted
audit_findings.magnitude: $434m, equal to 21.6% of the $2,008.1m anchor OE; if entirely recurring, approximately $6,098m or $23.15/share of base-case value
audit_findings.mechanism: Required contract-acquisition spending would be deducted from OE, with growth scenarios requiring enough reinvestment to obtain and retain contracts.
audit_findings.evidence: We capitalize direct costs that we incur to obtain contracts with customers, which we amortize on a straight-line basis over the initial term of the agreements, generally ranging from 15 to 30 years.
audit_findings.explanation: The $434m cash outflow is filed and its omission from the stated OE deductions is a demonstrated cash-flow mismatch. Whether all or only part is maintenance or growth investment remains unresolved, but the possible adjustment is large enough to change intrinsic value materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $434m by contract into maintenance, renewal and growth spending; then rerun every scenario with the recurring maintenance amount plus scenario-specific growth investment deducted from OE.

audit_findings.title: Current shares and debt are paired with stale interest expense
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt increased $711m from $16,204m at 2025 year-end to $16,915m at 2026-06-30; 2026 first-half interest expense was $435m versus $395m in the prior-year period; exact after-tax run-rate adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because debt principal is not deducted in the bridge, the OE numerator must contain the after-tax interest expense associated with the debt supporting the current equity claim and share count.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense increased primarily due to higher debt balances driven by Senior Notes issuances, net of maturities ($129 million).
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated, and stale interest would overstate equity OE. The filings do not establish the required adjustment because 2026 issuances, maturities, commercial paper, swaps and issuance timing must be modeled together. The observed increase indicates an effect, but the record does not establish materiality to value.
audit_findings.action: Build a 2026-06-30 debt-and-swap schedule, calculate annualized cash interest and tax effects, reconcile post-year-end repurchases to the selected diluted share count, and rerun using a date-consistent OE numerator and denominator.

audit_findings.title: A timing-driven reimbursement loss may be perpetuated
audit_findings.magnitude: $299m, equal to 14.9% of anchor OE; removing a wholly temporary deficit would add approximately $4,201m or $15.95/share to base-case value
audit_findings.mechanism: A normalized reimbursement adjustment enters OE by reversing timing-related expenses for which corresponding reimbursement revenue is expected, without adding genuinely unreimbursable costs.
audit_findings.evidence: Over the long term, our centralized programs and services are not designed to impact our economics, either positively or negatively.
audit_findings.explanation: The $299m FY2025 loss is demonstrated and materially depresses the anchor. Marriott states these programs are not designed to affect long-term economics, but that statement alone does not prove the entire amount is recoverable. The possible normalization is nevertheless large enough to change intrinsic value materially.
audit_findings.action: Trace the deficit through receivables, deferred revenue, loyalty liabilities and subsequent reimbursements; separate recoverable timing differences from recurring leakage and rerun OE using the supported normalized amount.

audit_findings.title: The anchor retains a one-off tax-reserve release
audit_findings.magnitude: $137m, equal to 6.8% of anchor OE; removing it would reduce base-case value by approximately $1,925m or $7.31/share
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonrecurring tax benefit inflates after-tax OE and is compounded through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our tax provision increased primarily due to higher non-U.S. taxes mainly from increased tax rates ($90 million) and higher pre-tax income ($62 million), partially offset by the current year release of tax reserves ($137 million).
audit_findings.explanation: Retention of the filed reserve release is a demonstrated normalization error if it was not separately removed. At 6.8% of anchor OE and about 6.7% of base equity value excluding rounding, it is material even though correcting it would not close the much larger gap between modeled value and market price.
audit_findings.action: Verify the OE tax reconciliation, remove the $137m benefit if still present, establish a sustainable cash tax rate including recurring jurisdictional costs, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified data-security claims remain ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Losses exceeding recorded accruals would reduce common-equity value directly or reduce future OE through settlement, legal, remediation and uninsured costs.
audit_findings.evidence: We are currently unable to reasonably estimate the range of total possible financial impact to the Company from the Data Security Incident in excess of the expenses already recorded; however, we do not believe this incident will impact our long-term financial health.
audit_findings.explanation: The litigation and an existing accrual are demonstrated, but the June 2026 filing says the excess loss or range cannot be reasonably estimated. The recorded accrual is described as not material, but that does not establish the scale of possible excess losses, so materiality remains unresolved rather than disproved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain subsequent mediation, litigation and regulatory developments, the recorded accrual, expected collectible insurance and remediation obligations; deduct the probability-weighted present value of exposure not already captured in normalized OE.

audit_findings.title: The citizenM earn-out is an omitted contingent claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $110m maximum, or $0.42/share undiscounted and 0.38% of the $28,676m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A triggered earn-out would be a scenario-linked cash claim deducted from the equity bridge or modeled as a future cash outflow.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, we may pay earn-out payments to the seller up to $ 110 million, based on the future growth of the brand over a specified, multi-year timeframe.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted contingent claim is demonstrated, but even the filed maximum before discounting is only 0.38% of base equity value. It therefore cannot materially change the valuation conclusion on its own, although scenarios benefiting from citizenM growth should recognize the matching payment.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that no earn-out liability is already captured, estimate trigger probability and timing, and include its discounted value as a citizenM-growth-linked bridge deduction for completeness.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $109m for FY2024, equal to 4.7% of FY2024 OE and 22.2% of filed D&A; if all were a recurring eligible add-back, approximately $1,531m or $5.81/share of base-case value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be non-economic and not duplicated by required capital spending would be added back to OE.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2024 $109.0m (22.2% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved classification possibility, not a demonstrated error, and its present treatment is conservative. Even treating the entire supplied FY2024 residual as a recurring eligible add-back would lift base value only about 5.3% and would not change the conclusion relative to the $336.07 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the filed component schedule for residual D&A, identify the corresponding assets and maintenance spending, determine the comparable FY2025 amount, and rerun only for components proven eligible and not offset by required reinvestment.
